descriptionChirho: Qal participle and infinitive used for skilled artisan work: to devise artistic designs in gold, silver, fabric, and stone, especially in the construction of the tabernacle (Exodus); includes the agent noun 'skilled craftsman, designer, inventor'.

Qal and Piel finite forms expressing cognitive activity: to think, ponder, consider, suppose, or form a mental judgment about a person or situation, without necessarily implying purposeful planning (Arabic فَكَّرَ/تَفَكَّرَ think, ظَنَّ suppose; Korean 생각하다 think; Swahili -fikiri think, -dhani suppose).

Qal and Piel active forms meaning to plan, devise, scheme, or plot, often with negative connotation of crafting evil or harm against someone (Arabic دَبَّرَ scheme; Korean 꾀하다/꿇하다 plot; Swahili -panga plan); includes participial agent nouns 'one who plots/devises'.

Qal and Piel forms with numerical or accounting sense: to reckon up, count, calculate a sum, keep accounts, or impute a quantity (Arabic حَسَبَ reckon/count; Korean 계산하다 calculate; Swahili -hesabu count).

Qal active forms expressing evaluative judgment: to regard, esteem, or consider someone or something as having a certain status or value; often with pronominal suffix indicating the object of regard (Arabic يَحْسِبُ regard; Korean 여기다 regard; Swahili -hesabu in evaluative sense).

Nifal (and Hitpael) passive and reflexive forms: to be reckoned, be counted, be regarded, be accounted as; the passive counterpart of both the counting and esteeming senses (Arabic يُحْسَبُ/حُسِبَ passive; Korean 여겨지다 be regarded; Swahili -hesabiwa passive of count).

Qal perfect forms expressing deliberate intention or divine/human purposing: to intend, purpose, or resolve upon a course of action, distinct from mere scheming by its emphasis on determined resolve (Arabic قَصَدَ intend/purpose; Korean 도모하다 plan with resolve; Swahili -kusudia intend).
